names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 23 Ιουνίου, «Άγιοι Αριστοκλής ο πρεσβύτερος, Δημητριανός διάκονος και Αθανάσιος αναγνώστης», which prints him as «Δημητριανός διάκονος»; the rank word is left off the stored form.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 20. јун ст. ст., „Свети мученици Аристокл, Димитријан и Атанасије“ — the second of the three bare forenames, with Свети and мученици off. „ђакон“ is in the body and not in the heading, so it was never a candidate for the form; «the Deacon» of the display name is the corpus’s own, off saint.gr’s heading. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Димитријан», which is worth having measured: the corpus keeps five Demetrianus folders, and none of them had an `sr` form at all.

Read out of the name link behind his place in days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 20 июня ст. ст., «Димитриан (Димитрий) Саламинский (Кипрский), диакон, сщмч.», with the grade and rank words left off; the parenthetical form and the epithets are the calendar's own.

death.note: Two books, two years, and the field is widened rather than chosen. saint.gr’s heading for each of the three: «(; - 302)», and its narrative «Το 302 μ.Χ.» for the year of the martyrdom. The Охридски пролог for 20. јун ст. ст.: „а Димитријана и Атанасија у огњу спале 306. године“ — Demetrian and Athanasius were burned in the fire in the year 306. Four years apart, nothing averaged and neither book preferred; the two books also disagree about the manner of the death, which is written in the life and in no field (5 October 2026).

feast.note: The same menologion number this folder's serbian row carries; its greek row stands on 23 June, which is that calendar's own day for the company and not a second Russian feast. The one life page days.pravoslavie.ru gives the three, life1352, heads «День памяти: 20 июня» and names no other day; it was read whole and its account agrees with what this folder already carries — Tamassos, the flight to the cave, the light and the command to return, the meeting at the church of the apostle Barnabas, the preaching at Salamis, the fire that did not touch two of them, and the beheading about 306 — so no paragraph was added. It names the persecution as that of Maximian Galerius, 305 to 311, and heads all three «Саламинский (Кипрский)» where this corpus has read the presbyter's own town, Tamassos, into the display names.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 20 июня ст. ст. — «Мчч. Аристоклия пресвитера, Димитриана диакона и Афанасия чтеца (ок. 306).»

attestations.note: Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 23ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιοι Αριστοκλής ο πρεσβύτερος, Δημητριανός διάκονος και Αθανάσιος αναγνώστης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 23 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and its own heading for him reads «(; - 302)». The entry names all three members, so it is one folder each, and the corpus already keeps the presbyter Aristocleus of Tamassos from the Romanian calendar on this day. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. He is not the corpus's `demetrianus-of-tamassos`, the presbyter of Tamassos whose Greek row is already venerated on 27 January; this man is the deacon of the church at Salamis, and the page's narrative calls him Δημήτριος once while its heading and the day's line call him Δημητριανός.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 03.07.2026 (20. јун ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Аристокл, Димитријан и Атанасије“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, the second of its three men. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The heading is quoted **whole** on all three folders, as §4 requires: a row’s quoted line is the Prologue’s own heading and not the part of it that names this man. **THE DAY IS NOT THE SAME NUMBER.** This folder’s only other venerated row is Greek and on **23 June**; this book keeps him on the **20th**. That is not a §4 second-day note — which is owed only where a folder already carries a venerated row for this same church on another day, and the `serbian` row was `undocumented` — and the row goes on the day of the page read. **THE DATE IS WIDENED.** The folder held `death` 302 to 302, display «302», off saint.gr’s heading «(; - 302)» for each of the three and its narrative «Το 302 μ.Χ.». This book says 306. Two books, two years, four apart, and the rule is to widen: `death` earliest 302, latest 306, display **«302 or 306»**, basis traditional, both sentences in the note. The «X or Y» form is right here and the dash form is not, because these are two readings and not a range either book states — the dash on `aristocleus-of-tamassos` today is there only because one of the two readings is itself a stated range. **THE MANNER OF DEATH DISAGREES, AND THIS IS THE FOLDER IT MATTERS MOST ON.** saint.gr beheads all three after many tortures. This book: „после истјазања Аристокла мачем посеку, а Димитријана и Атанасија у огњу спале“ — after the torments they cut Aristocles down with the sword, and **burned Demetrian and Athanasius in the fire**. One book has one death for three men, the other has two deaths for three men, and this man is on the side that moves. Both are written and neither is chosen. ONE NAME QUESTION THIS BOOK QUIETLY SETTLES NOTHING ABOUT. The folder records that saint.gr’s narrative calls the deacon **Demetrios** where its own heading and the day’s line have Demetrianus. This book prints Димитријан in the heading and Димитријана in the body, the same name twice, so **it agrees with saint.gr’s heading and not with saint.gr’s narrative** — which is recorded as a second book’s agreement and changes no field, §10 reserving display names and the stored form taking the heading’s word. `types` UNTOUCHED. Свети is not a rank, мученици is the rank and gives `martyr`, which is there. „ђакон“ stands in the **body** and a rank off a body is not written; `deacon` is on this folder already, off saint.gr’s heading, and is left as it was rather than confirmed from a body. No `office` — a deacon’s order is not a see, and no pack holds a phrase for it. No `locations`: Salamis and Tamassus are named in clauses and are not coordinates. **No new rows**, the three relating one another already. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE DAY’S FIFTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Свети Левкије, епископ врунтисиопољски, у Италији“ — Leucius, born in Alexandria, early into a monastery, counted worthy of great revelations and of a mighty grace, so that he raised the dead and drove demons out of men; bishop first in Alexandria, then by a command from heaven crossing into Italy to the pagan city of Vruntisiopolj, which he baptised whole and in which he built a church of the Mother of God; and after much and successful labour passing over into eternity in the time of the emperor Theodosius II, in the fifth century. **Three folders hold the name and not one of them is he.** `ls saints | grep -i leuci` returns exactly three: `leucius-of-caesarea`, a martyr of 249–251 kept with Thyrsus and Coronatus, who is not a bishop and not of Italy; `leucius-companion-of-peter`, a martyr kept with Peter and Severus on the Greek 11 January; and `leucius-of-volokolamsk`, a Russian. `ls saints | grep -iE 'brundis|brindis'` returns nobody at all. Ruling 3: named here, left out of every life written on this day, and no folder from me — and **the fifth century, Theodosius II and the city are written nowhere**, because there is nothing to write them on. The day’s verse is his, and a verse is not a hymn and not a folder either. THE DAY’S SIXTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Блажени Студије“ — Studius, a notable patrician and consul in Constantinople, who founded near the Golden Gate the church of Saint John the Forerunner and the monastery called the Studion after him; a house that became famous for many glorious men, spiritual fathers, ascetics and sufferers for the faith; destroyed by the Latin crusaders in 1204, restored by the emperor Constantine Palaeologus Porphyrogenitus in 1293, and with a Turkish mosque standing on the place now. `ls saints | grep -i studi` returns five folders and **every one of them is a Studite and not the Studius the house is named after** — `damascene-the-studite`, `james-of-studion`, `naucratius-the-studite`, `nicholas-the-studite`, `theodore-the-studite`. The last of those is the man this entry names as the house’s most famous son, and **he takes no row and no mention in any prose written today**: a founder’s monastery is a dedication and a later inhabitant of it is not a relation. Ruling 3 on Studius himself: named here, no folder from me, and **1204, 1293 and the consulship are written nowhere**. The Блажени of his heading therefore decides nothing, there being no folder for it to decide a type on; had there been one it would still be the §5 reading «fool-for-christ *or* righteous — read which», and a patrician and consul who founds a monastery is neither obviously.
